claims.text: A controlled post-fabrication heat treatment can induce coherent nanoprecipitates in a tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy.
The initial additively manufactured tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy is predominantly single-phase BCC.
Refractory high-entropy alloys can be fabricated using additive-manufacturing routes.
The heat treatment will produce a uniform, finely dispersed population of coherent nanoprecipitates.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces act as efficient sinks for irradiation-induced defects.
The nanoprecipitate interfaces promote recombination of irradiation-induced vacancies and interstitials.
Enhanced defect recombination limits helium-bubble nucleation and growth.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation motion or transmission.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces relieve stress concentrations associated with premature cracking.
Coherent nanoprecipitation can preserve a favorable combination of strength and tensile ductility in tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys.
Coherent nanoprecipitates will preserve strength and ductility after helium irradiation.
The heat treatment will enhance radiation tolerance under helium irradiation.
The heat-treated alloy will exhibit smaller helium bubbles than the as-fabricated alloy.
The heat-treated alloy will exhibit a lower helium-bubble number density than the as-fabricated alloy.
The heat-treated alloy will exhibit less irradiation-induced hardening than the as-fabricated alloy.
The heat-treated alloy will retain tensile strength comparable to the as-fabricated baseline after irradiation.
The heat-treated alloy will retain ductility comparable to the as-fabricated baseline after irradiation.
Helium-ion irradiation at approximately 900 °C and the unspecified reactor-relevant fluence is an appropriate condition for the proposed benefit.
A moderate nanoprecipitate volume fraction is beneficial, whereas excessive or inhomogeneous precipitation may negate the benefit.
The magnitude of improvement depends on heat-treatment parameters and the resulting precipitate characteristics.
